selected.rationale: The webapp→Ordering.API call is the synchronous checkout/order-placement path; 100% loss will hang or fail the user's order if no timeout/retry exists, exposing a missing-defense weakness on the core business edge.
This event-bus publish triggers the entire order workflow; losing the checkout message means no order is created and there is no visible recovery path, confirming an event-delivery/reliability gap.
The webapp's cart and checkout entry depend on Basket.API; loss makes the basket unavailable and may leave the UI hanging without degradation/fallback, exposing an availability weakness.
The mobile BFF path to Ordering.API carries checkout/order-status requests; loss here causes the same no-timeout/retry and availability failure as the web path but for mobile users.
OrderProcessor must persist status transitions; DB loss during processing leaves orders permanently in an intermediate state with no automatic retry, revealing missing recovery behavior.
PaymentProcessor's outbound event signals that payment completed; losing it stalls the entire order lifecycle and demonstrates missing ack/retry/outbox defenses on a critical event-bus edge.
Ordering.API's order-db dependency is on the critical write path for placing and querying orders; loss makes order creation fail and can leave partial data without recovery.
Identity.API is the synchronous authentication front-door for WebApp; loss blocks login/token operations for all users and reveals lack of fallback/caching for an identity dependency.
Basket state is exclusively stored in Redis; losing Redis breaks cart read/write and checkout, exposing missing cache-fallback/retry behavior in the cart service.
The webapp's product catalog is a synchronous user-facing call; service loss makes browsing unusable and exposes missing timeout/fallback on a high-traffic read edge.
